headline: High: shared filesystem and shell-capable slim can be steered by prompt-like content from awesome-prompts, creating injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can contain attacker-controlled instructions; slim reads files and processes stdin/stdout in an interactive CLI workflow. With a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge, slim could ingest prompt text as trusted instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is copied into slim's interactive prompt or command input, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, prompt text can be treated as trusted input.
mitigations: Keep prompt repositories and CLI sessions in separate directories.
Require a human review step before pasting any prompt text into slim.
Use a read-only mount for prompt sources.
Add a short allowlist for commands accepted by slim.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts itself has no network egress, but slim has broad network egress and handles filesystem artifacts plus registry credentials. If both touch the same workspace, slim can read and transmit files or secrets that were never meant for it. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly observed.
conditions: IF a shared workspace contains sensitive files, slim can read them.
IF slim is pointed at a directory with secrets or credentials, those contents may be exposed over network egress.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Remove secrets from any directory slim can read.
Run slim with a minimal input directory.
Rotate any registry credentials exposed to slim.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable content, while slim can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct write-write conflict, but if an operator places both in the same directory, slim's writes can overwrite prompt assets or generated artifacts. Uncertainty remains because the shared path is not documented, so the higher plausible severity is chosen.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, slim can overwrite files used by awesome-prompts.
IF the operator uses the same git checkout for prompt assets and container-analysis outputs, file conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Make the prompt repository read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared path.
Snapshot the workspace before running slim.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or per-agent sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt content that slim may treat as operational guidance if copied into its CLI workflow. slim then executes shell-capable actions and can act on that guidance without a verification layer. This creates a plausible cascade from content generation to action-taking, though the exact bridge is not documented.
conditions: IF prompt text from awesome-prompts is used as instructions for slim, slim may execute unsafe commands.
IF slim is allowed to act on unreviewed generated text, downstream actions can be wrong or destructive.
mitigations: Require manual verification of any generated instructions.
Disable shell execution for routine runs.
Use a checklist before copying text into slim.
Log and review all commands slim executes.
requires-engineering: add a policy gate between text generation and command execution.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository with no touched data classes, while slim handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, and environment variables. If the pair is used on the same sensitive workspace, slim can process regulated or secret material under a different handling model than the prompt repo. The compliance mismatch is inferred from slim's documented data classes.
conditions: IF slim is run against a workspace containing private keys or credentials, compliance obligations attach to that data.
IF prompt assets and sensitive container artifacts are co-located, retention and access controls may diverge.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of slim's input tree.
Use separate retention policies for prompt assets and container artifacts.
Document which directories may contain keys.
Purge temporary analysis outputs after each run.
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies across both workflows.
